description: Additional configuration for sending an alert to a generic webhook. The alert is sent as an HTTP POST, with a JSON body built from a template. The webhook URL and the header values are secrets: they are write only and are never returned.

body.description: The JSON body to send, as a Go template. It must render valid JSON of at most 64 KiB. Variables are written like {{.alert.alertDefinition.severity}}. Their values are escaped for the inside of a JSON string, so put them inside quotes; only the numbers (.alert.counter, .occurrences and .attempts) can be used without quotes.  The alert has the names of the Alerts API: .alert.ID, .alert.counter, .alert.start, .alert.end and .alert.alertDefinition, which has .name, .friendlyName, .severity, .message and .trigger (.occurrences and .interval). .alert.url is the link to the alert, and .platform.host is the host of the platform.  .alert.alertEvents lists up to 10 events, for {{range .alert.alertEvents}}...{{end}}. Each has .provider, .timestamp and .principal, which has .type, .teams, .user.name, .app.name and .app.component. .alert.dataSinkEvents lists the events of data sinks. Each has .dataSinkID, .dataSinkName, .dataset, .kind, .status, .runID, .backfillID, .attempts, .reason and .timestamp.  A field without a value is empty, such as .principal.user.name of an app. Inside a range, use $.alert or $.platform to reach the other variables.
body.title: body

headers.description: The HTTP headers to send with the request. Content-Type defaults to application/json when not set. There can be at most 20 headers, with distinct names. Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and Connection cannot be set.
headers.title: headers

webhookURL.description: The URL to send the alert to.
webhookURL.title: webhookURL
